steps.do: Read the summary line at the end of the test output.

K-017318.example: The test wraps a DropdownButtonFormField<String> in a Form whose validator returns 'Select a country' when value is null, then taps Submit. The expected result is exactly one 'Select a country' text in the widget tree after validate().
K-017318.check: Output ends with '+1: All tests passed!' and the failure count reads '-0'.
traps: Calling validate() without pumpAndSettle() reads stale state and can report a false pass.
Testing the validator function alone skips the Form wiring that displays the error text.
Using DropdownButton instead of DropdownButtonFormField leaves no validator hook.

steps.do: Run the analyzer on the select widget file.

K-017319.example: A DropdownButtonFormField<String> whose items are DropdownMenuItem<int> produces an analyzer error about the item type. After switching the items to DropdownMenuItem<String>, flutter analyze must report zero errors.
K-017319.check: Output is 'No issues found!' from both dart analyze and flutter analyze.
traps: Passing value: null to a non-nullable generic such as DropdownButtonFormField<String> is an analyzer error, so the field type must be String? when empty is allowed.
Analyzing only the widget file misses callers that pass mismatched item types.
Ignoring analyzer infos about deprecated DropdownButtonFormField parameters leaves the field broken on the next Flutter upgrade.

Assuming contrast passes from hex values without measuring the rendered result.

steps.do: Create src/ui/toast.rs and register it by adding a pub mod toast line to src/ui/mod.rs.

Run only the toast_rect tests.

K-017421.check: cargo test toast_rect prints 'test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed'.
traps: Rect::new takes x, y, width, height in that order, so swapping width and height gives wrong results.
Ratatui 0.28 and later use frame.area(), while older versions use frame.size(); check the version in Cargo.toml first.
Integer division on small widths can produce 0, so clamp the result to at least 1 before asserting.

steps.do: Add a function wrapped_height(message: &str, inner_width: u16) -> u16 that returns the ceiling of the character count divided by inner_width, with a minimum of 1.

Check the formatting of the toast module.
Run the wrapped height tests.

K-017422.example: A 21-character message in a box with 10 inner columns needs 3 rows, so the toast height is 3 plus 2 border rows. The single word ok needs 1 row.
K-017422.check: cargo test wrapped_height prints 'test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed' and rustfmt --check prints nothing and exits 0.
traps: Character counting ignores word-wrap breaks, so use messages without spaces in these tests and note that real text can wrap to more lines.
Forgetting the 2 border rows makes the toast clip its last line.
Passing the outer width instead of the inner width (outer minus 2) overestimates how many characters fit per line.

steps.do: Find any existing truncate helper so you do not write a duplicate.
Add a function truncate_toast(message: &str, max: usize) -> String that returns the message unchanged when it fits, and otherwise keeps max minus 3 characters and appends three dots.
Add a unit test named truncate_toast_long that asserts truncate_toast of Connection restored after retry with max 12 equals Connectio...
Add a unit test named truncate_toast_fits that asserts a 5-character message with max 12 is returned unchanged.
Run the truncation tests.

K-017423.example: With max 12, the message Connection restored after retry becomes Connectio... which is exactly 12 characters. A short message such as Saved is returned as is.
K-017423.check: cargo test truncate_toast prints 'test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed'.
traps: The result must be exactly max characters, so count the three dots as part of the limit.
Slicing a String by byte index panics on multi-byte characters, so use chars().take(n) instead.
Truncating before checking the length leaves a shorter message ending in dots when it should not be cut at all.

steps.do: Add a function max_visible(area_height: u16) -> usize that returns the smaller of 3 and area_height divided by 5.

Add a test named visible_count_short that asserts max_visible(12) equals 2 and max_visible(9) equals 1.
Run the visible count tests.
Confirm the whole file passes the formatter check.

K-017424.example: A 12-row terminal shows at most 2 toasts, because 12 divided by 5 is 2, while a 24-row terminal shows 3 because the cap of 3 applies. The queue keeps the rest for later.
K-017424.check: cargo test visible_count prints 'test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed' and rustfmt --check exits 0 with no output.
traps: Integer division rounds down, so 9 rows gives 1 and 4 rows gives 0; decide whether a zero count should hide the stack entirely.
Taking toasts from the front of the queue instead of the newest ones shows stale messages first.
Changing max_visible without updating the test constants makes the tests pass for the wrong reason, so keep the expected values written out.

Check the test clicks the toggle and expects document.documentElement.dataset.theme to be dark.
Check the test expects localStorage.getItem('app-theme') to be dark after unmounting and remounting the provider.

Confirm the lint run reports no errors or warnings.
